title: Imperial AI Policy Fellowship 2027: Apply for a 9-Month AI Policy Fellowship at Imperial College London
summary: The Imperial AI Policy Fellowship 2027 is a professional learning and development opportunity designed for senior civil and public servants who want to strengthen their understanding of artificial intelligence and its growing implications for public-sector policy, strategy, regulation, and service delivery. Delivered through the Imperial Policy Forum at Imperial College London , the Fellowship combines in-person learning, expert-led sessions, peer engagement, and an individual research project supported by academic mentors. The programme is designed to help participants move beyond theoretical discussions of AI and apply their learning to real policy challenges within their departments and areas of responsibility. Imperial AI Policy Fellowship 2027 Artificial intelligence is increasingly influencing how governments approach public services, regulation, infrastructure, healthcare, security, data, and strategic decision-making. For public-sector leaders, understanding both the capabilities and limitations of AI is becoming increasingly important. The Imperial AI Policy Fellowship provides an opportunity for senior civil and public servants to explore these issues in a structured environment while developing a research project connected to their own professional priorities. The 2027 Fellowship will run from February to October 2027 , with a total duration of nine months . Fellows will combine online learning and activities with in-person days at Imperial College London. Key Programme Details Programme: Imperial AI Policy Fellowship 2027 Institution: Imperial College London Duration: 9 months Programme dates: February–October 2027 Application deadline: Monday, 2 November 2026 Location: London and online Format: Individual research project combined with in-person days at Imperial College London Time commitment: Approximately 6–8 hours per month In-person commitment: Four in-person days throughout the year Fee: £1,500, with no VAT added What Is the Imperial AI Policy Fellowship? The Imperial AI Policy Fellowship is a bespoke learning and development programme aimed at senior civil and public servants seeking to develop their knowledge of artificial intelligence and understand how it can affect public-sector work. Rather than focusing exclusively on classroom-based learning, the programme combines structured learning with practical application. There are two main components. 1. In-Person Learning at Imperial College London Throughout the Fellowship, participants attend a series of in-person days at Imperial College London. These sessions are designed to help Fellows: Understand fundamental AI concepts. Examine how AI technologies work and what they are capable of. Consider the implications of AI for public policy. Explore AI-related strategy and regulation. Examine challenges associated with public-sector delivery. Engage with academics and specialists. Discuss ideas and experiences with other Fellows. Reflect on how AI knowledge can be applied to their professional responsibilities. The sessions include expert-led lectures, workshops, discussions and opportunities for interaction with peers and specialists. This structure means that participants are not simply learning about AI in the abstract. They are encouraged to think about how emerging technologies relate to actual policy questions and institutional challenges. 2. Individual Research Project The second major component is an individual research project or guiding question focused on a specific AI policy challenge. The project is Fellow-led , meaning that it is shaped around the participant s own policy priorities and professional objectives. Fellows receive support from one or more academic mentors who provide expert guidance throughout the programme. This allows participants to investigate an issue that is directly relevant to their area of work while benefiting from Imperial s academic expertise and institutional environment. The research component is therefore an important bridge between learning and practical policy development. What Can the Research Project Focus On? The Fellowship provides flexibility in the type of project participants can develop. Potential project formats include: Written recommendations for adopting AI within a particular part of a government department. Co-designing strategic plans or technical solutions for policy challenges. Piloting innovative or experimental AI applications within the public sector. Improving systems and infrastructure for AI, including data storage and management. Organising a facilitated workshop for colleagues within a department or team. Producing a published white paper. This flexibility allows Fellows to connect the Fellowship to real issues they are already encountering in their professional roles. Examples of Previous Research Projects The programme provides examples demonstrating how AI policy research can be connected to practical public-sector challenges. Previous examples include: AI and Food Regulation One project involved piloting an AI model for the Food Standards Agency designed to help organisations identify relevant regulations and the bodies responsible for those regulations. AI, Healthcare and Accountability Another project involved a paper co-written between the MHRA and NHS examining the accountability gap surrounding clinical negligence, product liability and practitioner literacy within the UK healthcare system. Human-Centred AI A collaborative workshop explored human-centred AI design involving the Home Office and Imperial s Collective Innovation Lab . AI and Defence Another example focused on Sovereign AI in Defence , involving Imperial academics, the Trusted AI Alliance and consultation with the UK Ministry of Defence. These examples illustrate the breadth of potential applications for AI policy research across government and public services. Benefits of the Imperial AI Policy Fellowship The Fellowship offers several forms of professional and academic development. Tailored Learning The programme provides a personalised learning experience based on Fellows individual needs and professional interests. This allows participants to focus their learning on issues that are relevant to their roles rather than following a completely generic AI curriculum. Practical Research Experience Fellows undertake a research project supported by an academic mentor. This provides an opportunity to apply AI knowledge to a real policy question and develop practical outputs that can potentially be useful within their departments. Access to Imperial Expertise Participants have the opportunity to learn from faculty and specialists associated with Imperial College London, including experts working across AI-related areas in engineering, medicine and science. Professional Networking The Fellowship brings together civil servants and public-sector professionals who share an interest in AI and related policy challenges. Participants can exchange experiences, develop professional relationships and learn from colleagues working on different policy issues. Public-Sector Focus The programme is specifically designed around the challenges of applying AI within the public sector. This means Fellows can explore questions involving policy, governance, regulation, strategy, implementation and public-sector systems rather than concentrating solely on the technical development of AI. Engagement with the Wider Imperial Community Fellows will also have opportunities to engage with the Imperial Policy Forum and the wider Imperial community. The programme combines these connections with formal learning and individual research, creating an environment in which participants can develop their understanding of AI while applying that knowledge to current policy questions. The Fellowship s activities have also included engagement with Imperial s AI and technology ecosystem. The programme information highlights Fellows visiting Imperial s biomedical engineering facilities and participating in workshops involving AI startups at the Deep Tech White City campus. Who Should Consider Applying? The programme is intended for senior civil and public servants who want to deepen their understanding of AI and its implications for public-sector work. It is particularly relevant to professionals who: Work on policy development or implementation. Have responsibilities involving technology or digital transformation. Work with AI-related regulation or governance. Are responsible for strategic planning. Work in public-sector innovation. Need to understand the implications of AI for their department. Want to investigate a specific AI-related policy challenge. Are interested in developing an evidence-based project connected to AI and public policy. The supplied programme information does not provide a specific nationality, race, or continent-based eligibility restriction. Therefore, those details should not be assumed from the available information. Time Commitment The Fellowship runs for nine months and requires approximately 6–8 hours per month . Participants must also commit to four in-person days throughout the year . The programme therefore combines ongoing engagement with concentrated periods of face-to-face learning at Imperial College London. Where Is the Fellowship Held? The Fellowship uses a hybrid format. Participants engage through: Online activities. In-person sessions. Individual research. Engagement with Imperial s academic and policy communities. The programme location is listed as London and online , with in-person days taking place at Imperial College London. Fellowship Cost The fee for participation in the 2027 Imperial AI Policy Fellowship is: £1,500 The programme information states that no VAT is added to this fee. Application Deadline Applications for the 2027 Fellowship are currently open. The application deadline is: Monday, 2 November 2026 Applicants are instructed to complete the application form and send it to the Imperial Policy Forum at the.forum@imperial.ac.uk . Applicants should therefore ensure that their application materials are completed and submitted before the stated deadline. How to Apply Prospective applicants should: Review the Imperial AI Policy Fellowship programme information. Consider how AI relates to their current public-sector responsibilities. Identify a policy challenge or research question that could form the basis of their Fellowship project. Consider what they hope to gain from the programme. Complete the official application form. Submit the completed application to the Imperial Policy Forum before the deadline. The official programme page provides access to both the programme brochure and the 2027 application form . Learn more and apply HERE Why the Research Project Matters A distinctive feature of this Fellowship is that participants are not simply passive recipients of training. The research project gives each Fellow an opportunity to connect their learning to a real-world policy challenge. For example, a participant could investigate how their department might adopt AI responsibly, explore policy requirements for a new technology, examine AI-related data infrastructure, develop recommendations for senior decision-makers, or design a workshop to improve colleagues understanding of AI. The project can therefore become a practical mechanism for transferring learning from the Fellowship into the Fellow s professional environment. A Fellowship Focused on Practical AI Policy The Imperial AI Policy Fellowship sits at the intersection of artificial intelligence, public policy and government leadership . As governments and public institutions consider how AI should be adopted, regulated and governed, public-sector professionals increasingly need the ability to understand both the opportunities and challenges associated with the technology. The Fellowship s structure responds to this need by combining: AI fundamentals. Policy analysis. Expert learning. Academic mentorship. Practical research. Peer exchange. Professional networking. Public-sector application. This combination allows Fellows to explore AI from both technical and policy perspectives while maintaining a strong connection to their professional responsibilities. Key Dates and Facts at a Glance Detail Information Programme Imperial AI Policy Fellowship Entry 2027 Institution Imperial College London Duration 9 months Programme period February–October 2027 Deadline 2 November 2026 Location London and online In-person commitment 4 days Monthly time commitment 6–8 hours Fee £1,500 Main participants Senior civil and public servants Main focus AI, public policy and public-sector applications Research component Individual Fellow-led project Academic support One or more academic mentors The programme details above are based on the supplied Imperial College London programme information. Conclusion The Imperial AI Policy Fellowship 2027 provides a structured opportunity for senior civil and public servants to deepen their understanding of artificial intelligence and examine how it can be applied to contemporary public-sector challenges. Running for nine months from February to October 2027, the programme combines in-person learning at Imperial College London, online engagement, expert-led sessions, peer networking and a Fellow-led research project supported by academic mentors. Participants can use the research component to explore practical questions involving AI adoption, policy development, regulation, public-sector systems, strategy and governance. With applications closing on 2 November 2026 , prospective applicants should review the programme requirements, identify a relevant policy challenge and prepare their application well before the deadline. title: Global Innovation Fellowships: Carnegie Endowment for International Peace 2026 – Up to £150,000 for UK-Based Researchers
summary: The Global Innovation Fellowships: Carnegie Endowment for International Peace 2026 provide an exciting opportunity for early- and mid-career researchers based in the United Kingdom to expand their professional networks, strengthen their research and policy engagement skills, and develop innovative responses to some of the world s most complex challenges. Offered by the British Academy in partnership with the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace , the fellowship is designed for researchers working across the humanities and social sciences who want to build stronger connections between academia, policymaking, and professional practice. The programme provides successful fellows with the opportunity to become embedded within the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace for a period of 12 months , with placements based in Washington, DC, Singapore, or Beirut , depending on the thematic area and proposed fellowship. With awards of up to £150,000 for 12 months , the Global Innovation Fellowships are intended to support researchers in developing new ideas, building international networks, translating academic knowledge into practical applications, and contributing fresh perspectives to policy challenges. The fellowship is particularly relevant to researchers interested in international affairs, global governance, climate and sustainability, geopolitics, Asian regional affairs, the Middle East and North Africa, international institutions, and other interconnected global challenges. Global Innovation Fellowships 2026 Overview The Global Innovation Fellowships are part of the British Academy s efforts to support researchers in the humanities and social sciences in developing relationships beyond traditional academic environments. The programme seeks to create opportunities where researchers can work directly with organisations operating in policy and practice. Through this approach, fellows can gain exposure to different perspectives and working environments while also contributing their academic expertise to real-world challenges. Key details of the 2026 fellowship include: Fellowship: Global Innovation Fellowships: Carnegie Endowment for International Peace Host organisation: Carnegie Endowment for International Peace Funding organisation: British Academy Career stage: Early-career and mid-career researchers Application status: Open for applications Opening date: 22 September 2026 Application deadline: 18 November 2026 at 17:00 GMT Interview date: 8 February 2027 Expected commencement: By September 2027 Possible earlier commencement: March or April 2027 Duration: 12 months Maximum award: Up to £150,000 Number of fellowships: Up to two Potential host locations: Washington, DC; Singapore; or Beirut Applicant location requirement: United Kingdom Academic disciplines: Humanities and social sciences Contact: international@thebritishacademy.ac.uk About the Global Innovation Fellowships The British Academy has received funding from the UK Department of Business, Innovation, Science and Trade to support its Innovation Fellowships programme. The Global Innovation Fellowships are intended to help researchers develop their skills, professional networks, and careers outside conventional academic environments. The programme places particular emphasis on creating connections between researchers and organisations in the creative and cultural, public, private, and policy sectors . The fellowship recognises that many of today s major challenges cannot be addressed effectively through a single discipline or institution. Issues such as climate change, sustainability, international security, geopolitical competition, global governance, technology, and regional political and economic transformation often require multiple perspectives. The programme therefore encourages researchers to bring their academic knowledge into a different professional setting while learning from practitioners, policymakers, and other experts. Partnership with the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace The fourth call of the Global Innovation Fellowships provides opportunities for selected award holders to become embedded within the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace . Carnegie is an international foreign policy institution whose experts work across different disciplines and regions on major global issues. Its work covers areas including democracy, technology, climate change, international affairs, and regional geopolitical developments. The fellowship is therefore structured to expose successful researchers to an environment where academic knowledge, policy analysis, international engagement, and practical problem-solving intersect. Depending on the subject of the fellowship, researchers may be hosted in Washington, DC, Singapore, or Beirut, with opportunities to engage with Carnegie colleagues and regional programmes. Main Objectives of the Fellowship The Global Innovation Fellowships are designed around a mutually beneficial relationship between the award holder and Carnegie. For fellows, the programme can provide an opportunity to: Develop new professional networks beyond academia. Strengthen connections with policymakers and practitioners. Translate academic research and expertise into practical applications. Develop innovative approaches to policy challenges. Gain experience working within an international policy organisation. Explore new perspectives on complex global issues. Strengthen professional skills relevant to policy and practice. Build relationships with experts working in different regions and disciplines. Increase the practical reach and impact of their research. Develop new collaborations that may continue beyond the fellowship. Improve their ability to communicate academic knowledge to non-academic audiences. For Carnegie, the fellowship provides an opportunity to benefit from the expertise, perspectives, research approaches, and experiences of researchers from the UK humanities and social sciences community. Research Areas for the 2026 Fellowship Applicants are invited to submit proposals in one of four broad thematic areas. 1. Sustainability, Climate and Geopolitics The first thematic area focuses on the interconnected challenges associated with climate change, sustainability, and nature . A fellowship in this area would be based in Washington, DC and would examine the relationship between environmental challenges and broader geopolitical developments. Applicants could explore issues surrounding the changing global environment, sustainability challenges, climate-related risks, geopolitical consequences, and innovative approaches to addressing interconnected environmental and international problems. The theme recognises that climate and sustainability challenges are not isolated environmental issues. They can intersect with economics, international relations, security, development, governance, resources, and global cooperation. 2. Global Order and Institutions The second thematic area focuses on questions surrounding global order, disorder, and international institutions . This fellowship would also be based in Washington, DC . Applicants working in this area could investigate different dimensions of the international system, including the functioning and evolution of international institutions, changing global relationships, international cooperation, and the challenges facing existing structures of global governance. The programme notes that there is no single solution to the challenges associated with global order and disorder. Applicants are therefore expected to bring thoughtful perspectives and potentially innovative approaches to understanding these developments. 3. South and East Asia The third thematic area focuses on South Asia, East Asia, and Southeast Asia . A fellowship in this area could be based in either Washington, DC, or Singapore , depending on the proposed work and engagement with Carnegie counterparts. Applicants should have strong expertise in one or more of these regions, including expertise relating to India or China and their regional or global roles. The programme is particularly interested in researchers who can contribute informed perspectives on the political, economic, social, strategic, and international dimensions of developments in these regions. Researchers may also engage with questions concerning the broader role of South and East Asian countries in international affairs. 4. Middle East and North Africa The fourth thematic area focuses on the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) . Fellows in this area would work with Carnegie s Middle East Program and could be based in Washington, DC, or Beirut . The fellowship may involve examining major challenges facing the region, long-term geopolitical trends, and possible innovative policy approaches. Applicants should have relevant expertise in the Middle East and North Africa, including the Gulf and Iran . The programme welcomes applicants with particular country or thematic expertise relating to political, social, or economic change. Academic and Professional Background The Global Innovation Fellowships do not prescribe one particular academic discipline. Applicants may come from a broad range of disciplinary, conceptual, and methodological backgrounds. The programme is open to perspectives that may be analytical, policy-oriented, practical, or combinations of these approaches. However, applicants must demonstrate a strong understanding of the issues relevant to their proposed fellowship, including the applicable policy environment and the systemic challenges associated with the subject. This means that applicants should be able to demonstrate more than academic interest in their chosen area. They should be able to explain the wider policy context and show how their expertise can contribute to understanding or addressing the challenges involved. Relevant language skills can be beneficial where appropriate to the proposed research or regional focus, although language skills are desirable rather than mandatory . Who Can Apply for the Global Innovation Fellowships? The programme is specifically designed for UK-based early- and mid-career researchers . To be eligible, applicants must meet several important conditions. UK Residency Applicants must be ordinarily resident in the United Kingdom . This requirement means that the fellowship is not a general worldwide opportunity open to researchers residing in any country. Current Long-Term Appointment Applicants must have a current long-term appointment that will continue for at least the duration of the fellowship award. The applicant must also be based at an eligible UK institution, such as: A Higher Education Institution (HEI); or An Independent Research Organisation (IRO). The institution must be listed as an approving organisation within the British Academy s Flexi-Grant system. If an applicant is successful, the institution will be issued the relevant terms and conditions associated with the award. Career Stage The fellowship is intended for: Early-career researchers; and Mid-career researchers. Applicants should therefore demonstrate an established connection to research as well as a clear rationale for how the fellowship will contribute to their professional development and future career. Humanities and Social Sciences Applicants should be researchers working within disciplines in the humanities and social sciences that are eligible under the British Academy s grant management system. There is no single required disciplinary background. The programme allows applicants to approach the thematic areas from different academic, methodological, conceptual, analytical, policy, and practical perspectives. Who Is Not Eligible? Postgraduate students are not eligible to apply for British Academy grant support under this programme. Applicants must confirm that they are not: Currently working towards a PhD; Awaiting the outcome of a viva voce examination; or Awaiting acceptance of corrections required by examiners. This is an important requirement for applicants who have recently completed or are close to completing doctoral studies. Applicants should carefully assess their status against these requirements before beginning an application. Collaboration Between Academia and Policy One of the central features of the Global Innovation Fellowships is the emphasis on moving knowledge between academic and non-academic environments. The fellowship is not simply intended to provide researchers with another academic research placement. Instead, successful applicants are expected to demonstrate how engagement with Carnegie can create value for both sides. Applicants should consider: How their academic expertise can contribute to Carnegie s work. What they can learn from working within a policy-focused organisation. How collaboration can generate new ideas. How their research can be translated into policy-relevant knowledge. How interaction with practitioners can influence their future work. How they can develop new professional networks. How their experience can contribute to their long-term career development. The programme particularly seeks applicants who are willing to explore perspectives outside their established academic environment. What the Fellowship Looks for in Applicants Successful applicants are expected to demonstrate an openness to new ideas and a willingness to experiment with innovative approaches. Important qualities include: Intellectual openness. Willingness to explore new perspectives. Interest in interdisciplinary engagement. Ability to work across academic and non-academic environments. Commitment to challenge-driven work. Interest in policy and practice. Ability to engage constructively with different perspectives. Understanding of the needs and priorities of the partner organisation. A clear interest in knowledge mobilisation and translation. A strong connection between the proposed fellowship and future professional development. Applicants should therefore carefully explain not only what they want to research or explore, but also why working with Carnegie is particularly valuable to their proposed project and professional trajectory. Fellowship Locations The location of the fellowship will depend largely on the thematic area and the nature of the proposed work. Possible locations include: Washington, DC Washington, DC is the proposed location for fellowships focusing on: Sustainability, climate and geopolitics. Global order and institutions. Some work related to South and East Asia. Some work related to the Middle East and North Africa. Singapore Singapore may host fellows working on South and East Asian issues. This provides an opportunity for researchers to engage with regional perspectives and Carnegie counterparts working on Asia. Beirut Beirut may host fellows working on Middle East and North Africa issues through Carnegie s Middle East Program. The location is therefore closely connected to the applicant s thematic expertise and proposed area of engagement. Fellowship Value and Financial Support The British Academy is offering up to two fellowships , each lasting up to 12 months . Each award can be worth up to £150,000 . The awards are offered with Full Economic Costing at 80 percent . The financial support is intended to facilitate a substantial period of engagement with Carnegie and enable successful researchers to undertake the fellowship in an international policy environment. Applicants should carefully consult the official scheme guidance to understand the eligible costs, institutional arrangements, funding conditions, and other financial requirements associated with the award. Fellowship Duration and Start Date The Global Innovation Fellowships are expected to commence by September 2027 . However, an earlier start in March or April 2027 may be possible. Applicants seeking an earlier start date will need to explain how they intend to manage the relocation process within the shorter preparation period. The standard fellowship duration is 12 months . Application Deadline The application deadline for the Global Innovation Fellowships 2026 is: 18 November 2026 at 17:00 GMT Applicants should avoid waiting until the final hours to submit their applications. It is advisable to review the scheme guidance, eligibility requirements, institutional requirements, and application materials well in advance of the deadline. Interview Date Applicants should also take note of the planned interview date. Interviews are scheduled for 8 February 2027. Applicants should ensure that they are available during this period if invited to an interview. How to Prepare a Strong Application Applicants interested in the Global Innovation Fellowships should carefully consider how their expertise, proposed area of work, and career objectives align with the programme. A strong application should clearly establish the connection between the applicant s background and the fellowship theme. Applicants should consider addressing the following areas: 1. Clearly Identify the Relevant Thematic Area Determine whether the proposed fellowship fits within: Sustainability, Climate and Geopolitics; Global Order and Institutions; South and East Asia; or Middle East and North Africa. The proposal should demonstrate a clear connection to the selected theme. 2. Demonstrate Relevant Expertise Applicants should explain their expertise and experience in the relevant area. This may include academic research, publications, policy engagement, professional experience, regional knowledge, methodological expertise, or practical work. 3. Explain the Policy Context The programme expects applicants to have a solid understanding of the relevant policy landscape. Applicants should therefore demonstrate awareness of the wider systems, institutions, actors, challenges, and policy debates connected to their proposed area. 4. Explain Why Carnegie Applicants should clearly explain why the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace is an appropriate partner for their proposed fellowship. The application should demonstrate how engagement with Carnegie could create opportunities for: Knowledge exchange. Collaboration. Professional development. Policy engagement. New research perspectives. Network development. Innovative approaches to complex challenges. 5. Demonstrate Value Beyond Academia Applicants should explain how their proposed fellowship could strengthen interaction between academic research and non-academic environments. This could involve showing how research findings might be translated into policy-relevant knowledge or how practical engagement could inform future academic work. 6. Connect the Fellowship to Career Development Applicants should demonstrate how the fellowship fits into their longer-term professional development. The programme is intended to help researchers develop skills, networks, and careers, so applicants should clearly explain what they expect to gain and how the experience could contribute to their future work. Important Eligibility Considerations Before applying, prospective applicants should carefully review the official scheme guidance. Particular attention should be paid to: UK residency requirements. Employment and appointment requirements. Eligible UK institutions. Career-stage requirements. Eligible disciplinary backgrounds. Postgraduate student restrictions. Current British Academy award restrictions. Carnegie s requirements for working at and with the organisation. Fellowship location and relocation considerations. The relationship between the proposed work and the selected thematic area. Applicants may not hold more than one British Academy award of a comparable nature at the same time. Previous Global Innovation Fellowship Awards The 2026 call represents the fourth call under this programme. Previous award holders and their projects are available through the British Academy s Global Innovation Fellowships past awards information. Reviewing previous awards can help prospective applicants understand the types of projects and approaches that have previously been supported. However, applicants should use previous awards as a source of context rather than attempting to replicate earlier projects. The current call has its own thematic areas, requirements, and application criteria. Why the Fellowship Is Relevant to Researchers The Global Innovation Fellowships offer researchers an opportunity to move beyond conventional academic boundaries and engage directly with an international policy organisation. For researchers whose work intersects with global affairs, international institutions, climate, sustainability, geopolitics, Asian regional affairs, or Middle Eastern and North African affairs, the programme provides an environment for developing connections between research and policy. The fellowship can also help researchers develop the ability to communicate complex academic ideas to audiences outside universities. This knowledge mobilisation and translation dimension is particularly important because research can have greater practical relevance when it is effectively communicated to policymakers, practitioners, institutions, and other stakeholders. Application Process Interested researchers should begin by reviewing the official fellowship guidance and eligibility requirements before accessing the application system. The general process involves: Reviewing the official Global Innovation Fellowships scheme information. Confirming eligibility. Identifying the most appropriate thematic area. Developing a clear fellowship proposal. Discussing the application with the relevant UK institution where appropriate. Reviewing the requirements for working with Carnegie. Preparing the required application information and supporting materials. Completing the application through the British Academy s application system. Submitting the completed application before the deadline. Preparing for the interview stage if shortlisted. Applicants should allow sufficient time for institutional processes and final application checks. APPLY HERE Official Application and Further Information Applications are submitted through the British Academy s grant application system. Applicants should also read the official scheme guidance notes and frequently asked questions before submitting an application. These resources provide additional information about eligibility, application requirements, the fellowship arrangement, and other programme conditions. Visit HERE to learn more about the Global Innovation Fellowships. Conclusion The Global Innovation Fellowships: Carnegie Endowment for International Peace 2026 provide UK-based early- and mid-career researchers in the humanities and social sciences with an opportunity to develop their professional networks, strengthen policy engagement, and explore innovative approaches to major international challenges. The programme offers up to two 12-month fellowships , with awards of up to £150,000 , and placements potentially based in Washington, DC, Singapore, or Beirut . The four thematic areas cover sustainability, climate and geopolitics; global order and institutions; South and East Asia; and the Middle East and North Africa. Because eligibility is specifically focused on researchers ordinarily resident in the UK and holding qualifying long-term appointments at eligible UK institutions, prospective applicants should carefully confirm their status before preparing an application. Researchers who meet the requirements and can demonstrate relevant expertise, openness to interdisciplinary perspectives, interest in policy engagement, and a clear rationale for working with Carnegie should review the official scheme guidance and prepare their applications well ahead of the 18 November 2026, 17:00 GMT deadline . title: Oxford Farming Conference Scholars Programme 2027: £1,000 Fully Funded Opportunity for Young People Under 30
summary: The Oxford Farming Conference (OFC) Scholars Programme 2027 is now preparing to welcome a new group of young people to one of the UK s leading agricultural conferences, offering participants an opportunity to develop professional skills, build valuable networks and engage directly with leaders and emerging voices across agriculture, food, business, science, technology and related sectors. The 2027 programme is particularly significant because it marks 25 years since the OFC Scholars Programme began . For its 2027 edition, the programme is being delivered in partnership with Severn Trent Water and M S , introducing a hybrid programme combining in-person gatherings, online learning and participation in the live Oxford Farming Conference in January 2027. Importantly, the programme is not restricted to people who have studied agriculture or currently work within the farming sector. OFC says it welcomes individuals from non-traditional sectors and backgrounds , as well as people with diverse geographical and academic experiences. Applicants who have never studied an agri-food subject are also encouraged to be considered. The programme is designed to help develop the future generations of agricultural and related-sector leaders , while giving Scholars access to peer networking, skills development, professional exposure and the opportunity to participate in discussions surrounding the future of agriculture. What Is the Oxford Farming Conference Scholars Programme? The Oxford Farming Conference (OFC) Scholars Programme is an initiative designed to support and develop young people who have the potential to contribute to the future of agriculture and related industries. Rather than simply providing conference attendance, the programme combines the main OFC conference experience with a wider programme of learning and networking activities. The 2027 programme will use a hybrid model , meaning Scholars will participate through a mixture of: In-person professional and educational events. Online bespoke sessions. Peer-to-peer networking. Skills development activities. The live Oxford Farming Conference. Exposure to people and organisations involved in agriculture and associated sectors. The programme is intended to provide participants with an opportunity to exchange ideas and perspectives while developing practical skills that can support their future careers and leadership ambitions. Oxford Farming Conference Scholars Programme 2027 Highlights The 2027 programme offers a number of significant benefits to successful Scholars. Key features include: Participation in the Oxford Farming Conference 2027 . Full conference access. Two nights of accommodation. Meals associated with the conference programme. Attendance at the Chair s Welcome Reception . Participation in the Oxford Union Debate . Attendance at the Christ Church dinner . Two dedicated in-person development and networking events. Bespoke online webinars. Peer-to-peer networking opportunities. Skills development training. Exposure to agricultural and food-sector leaders. Opportunities to meet people from different professional, geographical and academic backgrounds. The opportunity to become part of the OFC Scholars community. The programme is limited to a defined number of participants, making the application and selection process competitive. How Many Scholars Will Be Selected? For the standard Scholars Programme, 22 individuals will be selected. These places are funded by individual sponsors, who must nominate a proposed Scholar through the application process. In addition to the 22 standard Scholar places, the 2027 programme will include 8 Breaking Barriers places . The Breaking Barriers places are being funded by OFC, Severn Trent Water and M S and have a separate application arrangement. This means the 2027 programme is designed to provide opportunities for a broader range of young people, including individuals who may not traditionally have had access to major agricultural conferences or professional networks. Previous Oxford Farming Conference Attendance Applicants must also not have previously attended the Oxford Farming Conference . The Scholars Programme is intended to introduce new participants to the conference and provide them with an opportunity to experience OFC for the first time. Therefore, someone who has previously attended the Oxford Farming Conference would not meet the stated requirement for the standard Scholars Programme. Do You Need an Agriculture Degree to Apply? No specific agricultural academic qualification is stated as a requirement. This is one of the programme s key features. OFC explicitly encourages applications from people who have not studied agri-food subjects and says the programme welcomes individuals from outside the agriculture sector. This means that people with backgrounds in areas such as business, technology, science, policy, environmental studies, communications, economics, engineering and other disciplines may potentially be relevant to the programme, provided they meet the stated requirements and are put forward through the appropriate application route. The emphasis is therefore broader than academic agricultural qualifications alone. Who Can Sponsor a Scholar? The standard Scholars Programme uses a sponsor-led application model. According to OFC, any sponsor, organisation or group can apply for a Scholar place. The application must identify the proposed Scholar and provide information explaining: Who the proposed Scholar is. Their background and experience. Why they are suitable for the opportunity. How they are expected to benefit from participating in the programme. This makes the opportunity particularly relevant to organisations, businesses, professional groups and other bodies that want to support the development of a promising young person. How Does the Sponsorship and Funding Process Work? The standard Scholar places are fully funded by the applicant/sponsor . Sponsors submit an application on behalf of their proposed Scholar. The applications are then reviewed by the OFC Directors , with successful candidates offered a place on the programme. Importantly, a place is not confirmed until payment has been received . After an application is successful, the sponsoring organisation, group or individual will receive information about registration and payment. How Much Does the OFC Scholars Programme Cost? The cost of a Scholar place for OFC 2027 is: £1,000 excluding VAT The £1,000 cost includes a substantial package of conference-related benefits. According to the programme information, this includes: Two nights accommodation. The Chair s Welcome Reception. The Oxford Union Debate. The iconic Christ Church dinner. title: Denmark Scholarships for International Students: Erasmus Mundus, Danish Government Scholarships, Fulbright and Other Funding Opportunities
summary: Denmark offers a range of scholarship and funding opportunities for international students who want to pursue higher education, participate in student exchanges, or undertake research at Danish institutions. Funding opportunities are available through national and European programmes, institutional partnerships, exchange programmes, joint degree programmes and other international education schemes. For international students considering studying in Denmark, the available funding routes include Erasmus+, Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters, Nordplus, Fulbright Denmark, Danish Government Scholarships for highly qualified non-EU/EEA students, and the Danish State Educational Support (SU) , subject to the eligibility requirements of each programme. This guide explains the major scholarship and funding options, who can apply, what each programme supports, and where prospective applicants can obtain further information. Denmark Scholarships for International Students International students may be able to receive financial support to study in Denmark through several different programmes. However, there is no single application deadline covering all Denmark scholarships described below. Deadlines, selection procedures and eligibility requirements vary according to the programme, university and study programme. Some scholarships are designed specifically for exchange students, while others support students undertaking full-degree Master s programmes, research, or joint degrees involving Danish and other European institutions. The major opportunities include: Nordplus Erasmus+ Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters Fulbright Denmark Danish Government Scholarships for highly qualified non-EU/EEA students Danish State Educational Support (SU) Other European scholarship and research databases 1. Nordplus Scholarships and Study Opportunities Nordplus provides opportunities for students enrolled at higher education institutions in the Nordic and Baltic regions to study in another Nordic or Baltic country as part of their degree. The programme is therefore particularly relevant to students whose home institutions are located within the Nordic or Baltic region and whose academic programmes allow for international mobility. Students interested in using Nordplus to study in Denmark should first contact their home university or national educational agency to determine whether their institution participates in the relevant Nordplus arrangements. What does Nordplus offer? Depending on the applicable mobility arrangement, Nordplus can provide an opportunity to: Study in another Nordic or Baltic country. Complete part of an existing degree programme abroad. Gain international academic experience. Experience another higher education system. Participate in regional academic mobility. Students should not assume that simply being enrolled at a Nordic or Baltic institution automatically guarantees funding. The relevant institutional and programme requirements must be checked before applying. For additional information, prospective applicants can visit Nordplus . 2. Erasmus+ Study Abroad Opportunities The Erasmus+ programme provides opportunities for students from the EU/EEA and Switzerland to study abroad as part of their higher education in their home countries. According to the information provided by Study in Denmark, exchange periods can range from 2 to 12 months . This makes Erasmus+ particularly relevant for students who want to gain international study experience without necessarily completing their entire degree in Denmark. Who is Erasmus+ intended for? The programme described on the Study in Denmark scholarship page is primarily aimed at students from: EU countries European Economic Area (EEA) countries Switzerland Students normally participate through their existing higher education institutions rather than applying independently to Denmark as an entirely separate degree student. How does the Erasmus+ process work? Students interested in Erasmus+ should: Contact their home university. Determine whether their institution participates in the relevant Erasmus+ mobility arrangements. Discuss available destinations and study options. Confirm eligibility requirements. Follow the application procedure established by their home institution. Confirm the applicable mobility period and funding arrangements. The European Commission provides additional information about studying abroad through Erasmus+. Applicants can consult the European Commission Erasmus+ study-abroad information . 3. Erasmus Mundus Joint Master Degree Scholarships The Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters programme is one of the most internationally accessible funding routes connected with Master s-level study in Europe. Unlike some mobility programmes that primarily target European students, Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters are open to both EU/EEA and non-EU/EEA students . This makes the programme particularly relevant to international students from countries in Africa, Asia, the Americas, Oceania and other regions outside Europe, provided they meet the admission and scholarship requirements of the specific Master s programme. What is an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master? An Erasmus Mundus Joint Master is an international Master s programme delivered jointly by institutions in different countries. In the Denmark-related opportunities described by Study in Denmark, the Master s courses may be offered jointly by a Danish institution and another European university or higher education institution . Students therefore have the opportunity to participate in an international academic programme rather than studying exclusively within one institution or country. What can the scholarship provide? Depending on the individual Erasmus Mundus programme, scholarships may provide substantial financial support associated with participation in the Master s programme. However, scholarship conditions are not identical across all Erasmus Mundus programmes. Prospective applicants should therefore examine the individual Master s programme carefully to determine: Admission requirements Academic qualifications Scholarship availability Application deadline Required documents Selection criteria Mobility requirements Participating universities Study locations Financial support available How to apply for an Erasmus Mundus Scholarship Applicants do not generally apply through one universal Denmark scholarship application. Instead, students should identify an approved Erasmus Mundus Joint Master programme that matches their academic background and then contact or apply directly through the individual programme s official application process. The Study in Denmark information specifically advises students and scholars to contact the individual Erasmus Mundus Master s courses for details concerning scholarships and application procedures. A list of approved Erasmus Mundus Master s courses in Denmark is available through the EACEA Erasmus Mundus Catalogue . 4. Fulbright Denmark Grants The Fulbright Denmark programme supports educational exchange between the United States and Denmark and focuses on strengthening cultural and academic understanding through international exchange. The programme is particularly relevant to American scholars and postgraduate students at Master s or PhD level who want to undertake study and/or research in Denmark. What does Fulbright Denmark support? Eligible applicants can apply for a Fulbright grant for an entire academic year of study and/or research in Denmark . The programme can therefore be relevant to postgraduate students and scholars whose academic or research objectives align with opportunities available at Danish institutions. Who can apply? The information provided by Study in Denmark identifies: American scholars American postgraduate students Master s-level students PhD-level students as potential applicants. Applicants should consult Fulbright Denmark directly for the current eligibility requirements, selection criteria and application procedures. Further information is available from Fulbright Denmark . 5. Danish Government Scholarships for Highly Qualified Non-EU/EEA Students One of the most important funding routes for international students is the Danish Government Scholarships for highly qualified non-EU/EEA students . Danish universities receive a limited number of government scholarships each year to support highly qualified full-degree students from countries outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland. This means that the opportunity can be particularly relevant to international students from countries such as those in Africa, Asia, the Americas and other regions outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland , provided they satisfy the applicable requirements. Importantly, these scholarships are not necessarily awarded to every eligible student. Danish universities administer the scholarships and select the recipients. Eligibility for the Danish Government Scholarship According to Study in Denmark, applicants must meet the following conditions: Be a citizen of a country outside the European Union . Be from outside the European Economic Area (EEA) . Not be a citizen of Switzerland. Be enrolled in a full-degree higher education programme . Have been granted a time-limited residence permit in Denmark because of education . The scholarship is therefore different from an ordinary exchange arrangement because it concerns students pursuing a full degree programme in Denmark. Who is not eligible? Study in Denmark identifies several circumstances in which a student is not eligible for a Danish Government Scholarship. You may not qualify if you: Are seeking admission to an Artistic Higher Education Institution . Have a legal claim to the rights of Danish citizens. Hold a residence permit at the time of admission under the specific provisions described in the Danish Aliens Consolidations Act concerning certain family members of foreign citizens. Are eligible for a grant under the Danish State Education Fund. Because residence and immigration rules can be complex, applicants should carefully review the applicable requirements with their chosen Danish institution. Learn More HERE 6. What Does the Danish Government Scholarship Cover? The Danish Government Scholarship has two main components . It may consist of: A full or partial tuition fee waiver , and/or A grant toward living costs . Importantly, not every recipient necessarily receives the same combination or level of support. The exact scholarship arrangement depends on the Danish university administering the award. This is an important point for prospective applicants: being eligible for consideration does not necessarily mean receiving a full scholarship covering every expense. Students should therefore carefully review the scholarship information published by their chosen university. Learn More HERE 7. How the Danish Government Scholarship Application Process Works The scholarships are administered by Danish universities , which are responsible for selecting the students who receive the awards. Consequently, prospective applicants should not treat the scholarship as a single centralized national application. Instead, the recommended approach is to: Step 1: Identify a suitable Danish degree programme Applicants should first identify a full-degree programme that matches their academic background and career objectives. Step 2: Check the university s admission requirements Every university and programme may have its own academic and application requirements. These may include: Academic qualifications Previous degree requirements English-language requirements Programme-specific prerequisites Supporting documents Application forms Application deadlines Step 3: Check scholarship eligibility Applicants should determine whether their nationality and personal circumstances meet the Danish Government Scholarship requirements. Step 4: Review the university s scholarship procedure Because universities administer the scholarships themselves, prospective students should consult the admission and scholarship information provided by their selected institution. Step 5: Submit the required application Applicants should follow the university s instructions carefully and ensure that all required documents are submitted before the applicable deadline. The official Study in Denmark information on higher education institutions can be accessed through Study in Denmark s higher education institutions directory . 8. Is There a Deadline for the Denmark Scholarships? There is no single deadline for all of the scholarship opportunities described on the Study in Denmark page. This is because the opportunities are administered by different programmes, universities and organizations. For example: Erasmus+ deadlines can depend on the student s home institution. Erasmus Mundus deadlines are established by individual Master s programmes. Fulbright Denmark has its own application cycle. Danish Government Scholarship deadlines depend on the relevant Danish university and degree programme. Nordplus arrangements depend on the participating institutions and mobility procedures. Therefore, applicants should not rely on a single national deadline . Instead, prospective students should identify their preferred programme and institution and check its current official application deadline. For students considering the Danish Government Scholarship, this is particularly important because Danish universities determine their own application and scholarship procedures. Learn More HERE 9. Danish State Educational Support (SU) The Danish State Educational Support , commonly known as SU , is another source of educational financial support. However, international students should understand that SU is generally awarded to Danish residents . International students may nevertheless be able to apply for equal status for purposes of state educational support under certain circumstances. Equal status may be granted under: Danish rules European Union law This means that international students should not automatically assume that they qualify for SU simply because they have been admitted to a Danish university. Eligibility depends on the applicable rules and the student s individual circumstances. More information is available through the Danish Education Support Agency . 10. Other Sources of Scholarship Information for Studying in Denmark Students looking for funding to study in Denmark should also explore broader European scholarship databases. The Study in Denmark information points prospective students toward Ploteus , which lists scholarship programmes and educational opportunities for both EU and non-EU students. PhD students and researchers are also encouraged to explore the European Researchers Mobility Portal , now associated with the EURAXESS network. These resources can help prospective students and researchers identify additional opportunities beyond the scholarships administered directly by Danish institutions. Learn More HERE 11. Who Can Apply for These Denmark Scholarship Opportunities? Eligibility differs significantly depending on the programme. There is therefore no single nationality or academic qualification requirement covering all the opportunities. International students from outside Europe Non-EU/EEA students may be eligible for certain opportunities, particularly: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters Danish Government Scholarships for highly qualified non-EU/EEA students The Danish Government Scholarship specifically targets highly qualified full-degree students from outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland, subject to the stated conditions. EU/EEA students and Swiss students Students from EU/EEA countries and Switzerland can participate in certain European mobility programmes, including Erasmus+ opportunities described by Study in Denmark. They may also be eligible for Erasmus Mundus programmes, which are open to both European and non-European students. Students from Nordic and Baltic countries Students enrolled at Nordic or Baltic higher education institutions may have opportunities through Nordplus to study in another Nordic or Baltic country. American postgraduate students and scholars Fulbright Denmark is specifically relevant to American scholars and postgraduate students at Master s and PhD level seeking study and/or research opportunities in Denmark. 12. Academic Levels Covered The programmes described cover different stages of higher education. Undergraduate and exchange students Students participating in higher education mobility programmes may benefit from: Erasmus+ Nordplus The exact level and eligibility depend on the participating institution and programme. Master s students Master s-level students may find opportunities through: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters Danish Government Scholarships Fulbright Denmark for eligible American postgraduate students PhD students and researchers PhD students and researchers may find opportunities through: Fulbright Denmark European research mobility resources Individual Danish university opportunities Relevant Erasmus-related programmes The exact eligibility requirements should always be verified against the specific programme. 13. Important Considerations Before Applying Students considering studying in Denmark should carefully distinguish between admission , scholarship eligibility and scholarship selection . Being academically qualified for a programme does not necessarily guarantee a scholarship. Similarly, being eligible to apply for a scholarship does not necessarily mean that funding will be awarded. Applicants should consider the following: 1. Confirm your nationality eligibility Check whether your country falls within the programme s eligibility requirements. 2. Confirm your academic level Determine whether the opportunity is designed for undergraduate, Master s, PhD, exchange or research applicants. 3. Check whether the programme is full-degree or exchange-based Some opportunities support students completing part of a degree abroad, while others support students enrolled in a complete degree programme. 4. Check the specific university For Danish Government Scholarships, the individual university plays a central role in administering and selecting scholarship recipients. 5. Check the exact deadline Do not assume that all Danish scholarships have the same deadline. 6. Review funding carefully Determine whether the scholarship provides: Full tuition coverage Partial tuition coverage Living-cost support Exchange funding Research funding Other forms of financial assistance 7. Prepare documents early Depending on the programme, applicants may need academic transcripts, certificates, proof of language proficiency, motivation statements, research information, references and other supporting documentation. 14. Why Denmark Is an Attractive Destination for International Students Denmark has a broad higher education system offering hundreds of programmes taught in English. Study in Denmark indicates that Danish higher education institutions offer more than 500 English-taught study programmes . This provides international students with opportunities to search for programmes that align with their academic interests without necessarily requiring Danish-language proficiency for the programme itself. Students interested in studying in Denmark can explore available programmes through Study in Denmark s programme portal . 15. Useful Official Resources Prospective applicants should use official sources when researching scholarships because eligibility requirements, application procedures and deadlines can change. Erasmus+ European Commission – Erasmus+ Study Abroad Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters European Commission – Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters Erasmus Mundus Catalogue EACEA Erasmus Mundus Catalogue Nordplus Nordplus Official Website Fulbright Denmark Fulbright Denmark Danish State Educational Support Danish Education Support Agency Study in Denmark Study in Denmark Deadline There is no single overall deadline for these Denmark scholarship opportunities. Application deadlines vary according to the specific scholarship, university, degree programme or exchange scheme. Applicants should therefore check the official deadline for the particular opportunity they intend to pursue. For Erasmus Mundus, the deadline is determined by the individual Master s programme. For Danish Government Scholarships, applicants should check the deadline published by their chosen Danish higher education institution. Conclusion Denmark provides several pathways for international students seeking financial support for higher education, student exchange, postgraduate study and research. The opportunities range from Nordplus and Erasmus+ mobility programmes to Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters, Fulbright Denmark and Danish Government Scholarships for highly qualified non-EU/EEA students . One of the most important points for prospective applicants is that these programmes do not operate under one common application system. Each programme has its own eligibility requirements, application procedure, funding structure and deadline. Danish Government Scholarships, in particular, are administered by individual Danish universities, meaning that students must consult the institution and degree programme they are interested in for precise scholarship information. International students should therefore begin by identifying an appropriate study programme, checking whether they meet its academic and nationality requirements, reviewing the available funding options, and then following the official application procedure. For students from outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland, the Danish Government Scholarship and Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters can provide important potential routes to funded Master s-level study, while exchange students and eligible European students may find opportunities through Erasmus+ and Nordplus. American postgraduate students and scholars can also explore Fulbright Denmark for study and research opportunities. Because deadlines and requirements can change, applicants should always verify the latest information directly with the relevant Danish university, programme administrator or official scholarship provider before submitting an application.
