title: GFF x CIVIC VOICES Call for Proposals 2026: Up to US$175,000 for Civil Society and Youth-Led Organizations in Africa
summary: Applications are open for the GFF x CIVIC VOICES Call for Proposals 2026 , supporting local civil society organizations (CSOs) and youth-led organizations (YLOs) to strengthen civic engagement, health financing advocacy and accountability for reproductive, maternal, newborn, child, and adolescent health plus nutrition (RMNCAH+N). The VOICES (Voices Organizing for Inclusive Civic Engagement and Sustainability) initiative will provide grants of up to US$175,000 to eligible country partnerships across 22 African countries , with a total funding envelope of US$3.35 million . Civil society and youth-led organizations are essential partners in improving health and nutrition outcomes for women, children, and adolescents. Yet too often, barriers to participation limit their influence. The World Bank Group’s GFF × CIVIC partnership —a joint initiative of the Global Financing Facility for Women, Children and Adolescents (GFF) and the CIVIC: The Civil Society and Social Innovation Alliance —works to help close that gap. Through its first pillar, the initiative is supporting a consortium led by PATH—in partnership with the African Institute for Development Policy (AFIDEP) and the Organisation of African Youth (OAY), working together as VOICES (Voices Organizing for Inclusive Civic Engagement and Sustainability)—to strengthen civil society engagement, coalition-building, and youth leadership around domestic resource mobilization for women’s, children’s and adolescent health and nutrition. To advance these objectives, the VOICES consortium will award subgrants to local CSOs and youth-led organizations in up to 22 African countries. GFF x CIVIC VOICES Call for Proposals 2026 Working together as the VOICES consortium, PATH, AFIDEP, and OAY are implementing Pillar 1 of the GFF x CIVIC Platform in up to 22 African countries. The project supports GFF x CIVIC’s aim of empowering CSOs and YLOs to drive better health and nutrition outcomes for women, children, and adolescents by strengthening their role in influencing health financing, policy, and service delivery, with specific goals to boost domestic resource mobilization and scale innovative community-led solutions. GFF x CIVIC VOICES responds to persistent gaps in health financing, accountability, and civic participation by improving coordination and alignment among CSOs and YLOs and strengthening their capacity to engage more effectively in government-led planning, budgeting, and accountability processes. The project also seeks to deepen and institutionalize civil society and youth engagement in World Bank-supported processes at the country level, ensuring that health policies and financing decisions are informed by robust evidence, lived experience, and citizen voice. Key Details Details Information Release date September 15, 2026 Proposal deadline October 7, 2026; 23:59 EAT Total funding US$3,350,000 Grant size US$150,000–US$175,000 Expected awards 22 Award start date November 30, 2026 Grant duration Up to 18 months Issuing organization PATH Funder Global Financing Facility and The Civil Society and Social Innovation Alliance (GFF x CIVIC) Application languages English, French or Portuguese Email voices@path.org Eligible Countries Organizations from the following countries are eligible to apply: Burkina Faso Cameroon Central African Republic (CAR) Chad Cote d’Ivoire Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) Ethiopia Ghana Guinea Kenya Liberia Malawi Mali Mozambique Nigeria Rwanda Senegal Sierra Leone Tanzania Uganda Zambia Zimbabwe The call anticipates 22 awards , with one local partnership selected in each country, subject to the quality of proposals received. About GFF x CIVIC VOICES VOICES (Voices Organizing for Inclusive Civic Engagement and Sustainability) is the consortium made up of PATH, AFIDEP, and OAY that is implementing Pillar 1 of GFF x CIVIC to strengthen coordinated civil society and youth advocacy for increased domestic investment and accountability for RMNCAH+Nutrition. Across Africa, chronic underinvestment and weak health systems continue to undermine progress in reproductive, maternal, newborn, child, and adolescent health plus nutrition (RMNCAH+N). Preventable mortality and morbidity among women, children, and adolescents remain unacceptably high, with the burden concentrated in a limited number of countries. These challenges are intensifying as external health financing declines. Recent estimates suggest Official Development Assistance (ODA) for health between fell by 23% in 2025, widening domestic financing gaps at a time when health needs are growing. Data from 12 GFF partner countries reveals a crisis of unprecedented scale: 86 percent of surveyed organizations reported national-level ODA disruptions, while 93 percent experienced direct organizational impact, underscoring that funding instability is no longer episodic but systemic. Purpose of the Call for Proposals The purpose of this Call for Proposals is to identify and support partnerships of local CSOs and YLOs/networks/coalitions in each target country to design and implement coordinated advocacy and civic engagement interventions toward increased domestic investment and accountability for RMNCAH+N. Interested parties are required to submit together in a consortium, referred to as the “LCYO country partnerships,” of a maximum of three (3) organizations that includes at least one CSO and one YLO. Only one local partnership will be selected in each country. The successful LCYO country partnerships will receive training and technical assistance to advance their advocacy plans with the aim of moving beyond fragmented, organization-led projects toward sustained, coalition-driven advocacy within formal decision-making spaces. Scope of the Project Proposals must address two objectives. Priority Area 1: Strengthen Coordination and Alignment Strengthen coordination and alignment among civil society and youth-led advocacy actors working on RMNCAH+N. Under this objective, the selected country partnership will, among other things: Establish or strengthen coordination mechanisms among RMNCAH+N CSOs, YLOs, coalitions, and networks in the country. Support creation of joint advocacy agendas, messaging, and action plans aligned to national priorities as defined in relevant policy documents, including the RMNCAH+N Investment Cases and Country Partnership Frameworks. Strengthen inclusive civic engagement, including engagement of youth and community-led groups, in domestic resource mobilization for RMNCAH+N. Support community voices, including youth, to influence policy and financing decisions. Priority Area 2: Advocate for Increased Domestic Resource Investment Advocate for increased domestic resource investment and accountability for RMNCAH+N at national and/or subnational levels. Under this objective, the selected country partnership will, among other things: Conduct advocacy targeting national and/or subnational planning, budgeting, and financing processes, including those supported by GFF, such as RMNCH+N Investment Cases, Country Partnership Frameworks, and Multi-stakeholder Platforms. Package and disseminate evidence, with technical assistance from the VOICES consortium, to inform advocacy to increase public investment for RMNCAH+N. Participate in government-led policy, planning, and accountability platforms, such as technical working groups. Track commitments and support civil society oversight of RMNCAH+N investments. Document lessons learned, good practices, and advocacy outcomes. Contribute to cross-country learning agendas. These illustrative activities will contribute to the GFF x CIVIC VOICES’ expected outcomes of strengthening capacities of LCYOs on health financing and accountability to support advocacy on domestic resource mobilization for women, children, and adolescent health and improving meaningful LCYO engagement in government-led processes, including GFF and World Bank Group-supported activities, on women’s, children’s, and adolescent health. Selected country partnerships will contribute to monitoring, evaluation, and learning (MEL) focused on evaluating these outcomes and share learnings with country partnerships from the other 21 countries. Intended Impact Through this project, LCYOs are empowered, resourced, and institutionalized within decision-making structures to influence domestic resource mobilization and accountability , with the aim toward increased and more equitably allocated, sustainable, and youth-responsive domestic RMNCAH+N investments. Funding Available The maximum amount to be awarded to LCYOs for this Call is US$3,350,000 in up to 22 countries . The call anticipates awarding one grant in each country, but this will be dependent on the quality of proposals received. The maximum grant size for each award, for up to 18 months, will be: Up to US$150,000 for Burkina Faso, Cameroon, CAR, Chad, Cote d’Ivoire, DRC, Ethiopia, Ghana, Guinea, Liberia, Malawi, Mali, Mozambique, Rwanda, Sierra Leone, Tanzania, Uganda, Zambia, and Zimbabwe. Up to US$175,000 for Kenya and Nigeria, where, in order to make meaningful change due to the decentralized health budget, the proposals should include subnational advocacy engagement. Please note: The VOICES consortium reserves the right to modify this as needed and based on proposals received. All parties will be notified of any changes simultaneously. Eligibility Requirements Composition of LCYO Partnerships Applicants must meet the following requirements: Applications must be submitted on behalf of an LCYO representing a partnership composed of at least two (2) and no more than three (3) local organizations, one of which must be a youth-led organization (YLO). Each LCYO country partnership must designate a lead organization, which will hold legal, financial, and programmatic responsibility for grant implementation and management. The lead organization will receive funds and should have the capacity to subgrant to the other members of the partnership, where necessary. The lead organization must have a minimum of five (5) years of experience in health financing advocacy and accountability for RMNCAH+N, while partner organizations must each have at least three (3) years of relevant experience in health advocacy. All LCYO country partnership members must be local organizations/networks/coalitions that are legally registered and operational in the country of implementation. LCYO country partnership members should demonstrate complementary strengths across advocacy and policy engagement, budget analysis and tracking, youth engagement, community engagement, and coalition building. An organization can only apply under one LCYO country partnership application. To ensure broad and equitable access to the available funding, CSOs and YLOs selected to receive a grant under Pillar 1 will not be eligible to receive funding under Pillar 2 of the GFF x CIVIC funding opportunity. Organizational Requirements for the Lead Organization The lead organization must be: Legally registered and operating in accordance with applicable laws and regulations. Compliant with statutory obligations, including submission of annual returns and regulatory filings. Equipped with sound legal capacity to enter into contractual agreements and receive and manage grant funds. Demonstrating compliance with labor laws and fair employment practices that promote safe, inclusive, and non-discriminatory work environments. Operating with functional governance and organizational structure with defined roles, responsibilities and reporting lines. Equipped with well-documented operational policies and procedures adequate for effective project execution. Demonstrating institutional continuity and capacity not dependent on a single individual. Implementing programs aligned with organization’s mandate, strategy, and national priorities. The lead organization should also have: Well-maintained systems for planning and MEL. Demonstrated capacity to track results, document outcomes, and report on performance. Readiness to undergo a due diligence process, including a rapid pre-award assessment. MOUs or current projects with local authorities and other relevant bodies, which would be an added advantage. Finance and Administrative Requirements For the lead organization: Demonstrated experience managing donor-funded projects transparently and in accordance with fiduciary requirements. Existence of a functional financial management and reporting system. Effective internal controls system, including segregation of duties and authorization procedures. Demonstrated capacity to prepare and manage budgets and monitor expenditures against plans. Evidence of having undergone independent external audits and addressed audit findings in a reasonably timely manner. Demonstrated capacity to pre-finance start-up activities depending on the subgranting mechanism that will be agreed upon. Adequate, qualified, and experienced personnel and administrative capacity to implement the proposed activities. Where applicable, applicants may be asked during due diligence process to provide official documentation from the relevant government ministry or regulatory authority confirming their eligibility to receive external or foreign funding. Technical and Programmatic Requirements Across the partnership, applicants should demonstrate: Experience in advocacy, civic engagement, or accountability related to RMNCAH+N. Experience engaging government institutions and development partners, including GFF and/or World Bank country teams on policy, planning, or budget processes. Experience working in coalitions or networks is strongly preferred. Demonstrated commitment to gender equality, youth engagement, and inclusion. Strong local presence and experience implementing projects and programs, particularly involving women, youth, and children. Experience engaging with governments and local stakeholders on RMNCAH+N in general. Active membership in local platforms and/or coalitions such as the RMNCAH+N CSO platform, Multi-Stakeholder Platform, MOH RMNCAH+N technical working groups is an added advantage. Ability to demonstrate programming and impact, for example through programmatic reports, annual workplans, and budgets from within the past two years. Proposal Submission Requirements Applicants should submit the following: Submission template that has been provided — must be submitted as a Word document. High-level budget using the template provided — must be submitted as an Excel document. Proof of legal registration for each partnership member — PDF or JPEG. Budget verification for lead organization — PDF or JPEG. Organizational organogram , for all partnership members if possible — PDF or JPEG. How to Apply Submission Instructions 1. Language: This Call for Proposal has also been provided in English, French and Portuguese to facilitate broad participation across eligible countries. Applicants may submit their proposals in any of these three languages. 2. Email submission: All application documents should be submitted via email to voices@PATH.org . 3. Deadline: The submission due date and time is October 7, 2026, 23:59 EAT . 4. File formats: Documents must be submitted in the prescribed formats outlined in the submission and budget templates. 5. Attachment size: To ensure delivery, please ensure your attachments do not total more than 150 MB . If necessary, you may send the PDF and JPEG attachments as a separate email. 6. Confirmation: You will receive an automated response when your email has been received. Evaluation Criteria Proposals received by the deadline will undergo a layered and weighted review process, comprising an initial eligibility screening, technical assessment, and final selection. Eligible proposals will be scored against pre-defined evaluation criteria, with each criterion assigned a specific weight to reflect its relative importance to the GFF x CIVIC VOICES objectives. The weighted assessment will inform the shortlisting and final selection of applicants. Evaluation Criteria Percentage Relevance and strategic focus of the proposed approach 25% Advocacy experience and capacity of the LCYO country partnership members 25% Cost-effectiveness and realism of the proposed budget 10% Financial and grant management capacity 10% Integration of social equity and gender considerations 10% Sustainability 10% Innovation 10% Important Notes PATH, in consortium with AFIDEP and OAY: Will serve as the consortium fiduciary and will disburse and manage all subgrants. Will not be responsible for any costs incurred by applicants in the preparation or submission of proposals. Reserves the right to accept or reject any or all proposals at its sole discretion. Reserves the right to negotiate final terms, costs, and scope of work with selected applicants, including the substance of proposals, the inclusion or exclusion of specific components, and the involvement of third parties. Acceptance of a proposal does not constitute acceptance of its terms and conditions. Reserves the right to reject any and all proposals received in response to this call and is in no way bound to accept any proposal. Key Dates Event Timeline Call for Proposals release date and launch event September 15, 2026 Deadline for clarifying questions September 21, 2026 Responses to clarifying questions September 25, 2026 Proposals due October 7, 2026, 23:59 East Africa Time Targeted date for evaluation of all submitted proposals October 27, 2026 Public announcement of selected country partnerships November 30, 2026 The call notes that the VOICES consortium reserves the right to modify the schedule as needed , with all parties to be notified simultaneously by email. title: PAID FAO Internship Programme 2027: Gain Hands-On Experience with the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization
summary: Internship Programme The Internship Programme is a learning opportunity aimed at attracting talented young women and men who are strongly motivated to share their new perspectives, innovative ideas and latest research experience in FAO’s domains. The Internship Programme provides selected students, enrolled in an under-graduate or post-graduate degree programme or recent graduates, with the opportunity to supplement their academic knowledge with a practical work experience in a field related to the work of FAO. It will enable them to gain a better understanding of FAO’s mandate and programmes. At the same time, the Programme provides FAO with the assistance of qualified individuals specializing in relevant fields in connection to FAO Strategic Objectives and to UN Sustainable Development Goals . About the FAO Internship Programme The FAO Internship Programme provides selected undergraduate and postgraduate students — or recent graduates — the chance to complement their academic learning with meaningful, practical experience in areas related to FAO’s mandate. Interns work alongside experts on projects that promote sustainable food systems, environmental protection, and global nutrition security. Through this experience, interns deepen their understanding of FAO’s global role in eradicating hunger and supporting sustainable livelihoods, while FAO benefits from the enthusiasm, knowledge, and innovative thinking that interns bring to the organization. Eligibility Criteria Nationality : candidates must be nationals of FAO Members . Education : candidates must be students enrolled in an under-graduate or graduate degree programme in a bona fide educational institution at the time of application, or recent graduates. Applicants pursuing their studies in a country where higher education is not divided into under-graduate and graduate stages must have completed at least three years of full-time studies towards the completion of a degree. Languages : candidates must have working knowledge of at least one FAO official language (English, French, Spanish, Arabic, Chinese or Russian). Knowledge of a second FAO official language will be considered an asset. Age : candidates should be aged between 21 and 30 at the start of their internship (i.e. internship should start before the candidate turns 31). Skills : candidates should be able to adapt to an international multicultural environment, have good communication skills and be knowledgeable in the use of basic computer programmes. Residence/Visa status : candidates should have appropriate residence or immigration status in the country of assignment prior to the start of the internship assignment. Family relation : candidates with family members (defined as brother, sister, mother, father) employed by FAO under any type of contract are not eligible for the Internship Programme. Internship Duration The duration of an FAO internship typically ranges from 3 to 11 months , depending on the assignment and department needs. Living in the Duty Station Once selected, FAO interns receive a monthly stipend in local currency, not exceeding US$700 , to support living expenses. Sponsored interns receive their financial support directly from their sponsoring institutions. How to Apply Apply to the “Call for Expression of Interest”, which is published on our career portal. title: 10 Fully Funded PhD Positions in Urban Health at the University of Bonn, Germany – Urban Future Research Training Group 2027
summary: The University of Bonn and Bonn-Rhein-Sieg University of Applied Sciences are inviting applications for 10 doctoral research positions under the DFG Research Training Group (RTG) “Urban Future – Managing Transformations for Better Health in Blue Cities.” The interdisciplinary doctoral programme focuses on the relationship between urbanisation, water, public health, ecological sustainability and social justice , with particular attention to cities located along rivers and coastlines. Starting in April 2027 , successful candidates will join a structured four-year doctoral programme that combines individual PhD research with interdisciplinary training, seminars, systems-thinking approaches, transdisciplinary research methods and professional development. The programme is particularly relevant to graduates interested in urban health, public health, climate change, water-health systems, governance, environmental sustainability, infectious diseases, urban planning, ecological systems, development studies and social sciences . Successful doctoral researchers will receive a four-year doctoral support contract with remuneration based on TV-L pay grade 13 (65%) , according to the German public-sector salary scale. Employment will be at either the University of Bonn or Bonn-Rhein-Sieg University of Applied Sciences. The application deadline is 19 October 2026 . About the Urban Future Research Training Group The DFG Research Training Group “Urban Future” examines how cities can manage urban transformations in ways that improve public health, ecological sustainability and social equity . The programme uses the concept of the “Blue City” to describe urban areas situated along rivers or coastlines where water is considered more than simply a resource or a potential hazard. Instead, water becomes an integral part of: Urban planning Infrastructure development Environmental management Public health Social systems Urban identity Climate adaptation Ecological sustainability The research programme recognises that cities are complex systems in which environmental, social, economic, political and health-related factors interact. Researchers will therefore investigate the connections between urban transformation, water-related challenges and health outcomes , particularly in rapidly changing urban environments. A major emphasis is placed on cities in the Global South , which serve as important living laboratories for understanding urban transformation and developing solutions that can contribute to healthier and more sustainable cities. However, applicants are not restricted to research sites in the Global South. Candidates are free to propose research sites in any Blue City worldwide , provided that the proposed research aligns with the objectives of the programme. Universities and International Research Network The Research Training Group is jointly operated by: University of Bonn Bonn-Rhein-Sieg University of Applied Sciences It works in cooperation with the German Institute of Development and Sustainability (IDOS) and a network of international partner universities. The international partnership includes institutions in: Ghana Togo Cameroon Brazil Japan The listed partner institutions include: KNUST – Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, Ghana University of Ghana, Ghana University of Cape Coast, Ghana University of Lomé, Togo University of Buea, Cameroon University of São Paulo, Brazil The University of Tokyo, Japan This international structure gives doctoral researchers an opportunity to work within a research environment that connects European and Global South perspectives on urban health, sustainability and transformation. Four Research Themes of the Urban Future PhD Programme The doctoral programme is organised around four major interdisciplinary research themes. Research Theme A: Urban Health Resilience The Urban Health Resilience theme examines how urban communities respond to and recover from health pressures associated with water and environmental change. Research may focus on issues such as: Flooding Drought Urban heat islands Air pollution Unequal access to clean water Food systems Environmental exposures Mental health Social inequalities Climate adaptation Green and blue infrastructure The research theme combines perspectives from areas such as epidemiology, sociology, environmental science, urban planning and public health . Researchers will examine how communities can develop greater resilience while ensuring that vulnerable populations are not left behind. Example PhD research topics Potential research areas include: Urban Food Systems Possible methods include: Nutritional analysis Dietary surveys Health outcome measurements Intervention studies Soil Health and Soil Functions Potential methods include: Soil surveys Soil health indicator measurement Ecosystem measurements Functional measurements One Health and Planetary Health Resilience Potential methods include: Human and mental health assessments Environmental exposure measurements Longitudinal studies Spatial analysis Socio-ecological analysis Intervention and transformative studies Urban Blue and Green Infrastructure Potential methods include: Health impact assessments Human and mental health assessments Environmental exposure measurements Knowledge, Attitudes and Practices (KAP) surveys Perception surveys Spatial analysis Ecosystem services accounting Potential supervisors Research Theme A includes supervision from: Prof. Dr. Ina Danquah PD Dr. Timo Falkenberg Prof. Dr. Martin Hamer Prof. Wiltrud Terlau Prof. Dr. Mariele Evers Research Theme B: Urban Disease Ecology The Urban Disease Ecology theme explores how environmental and ecological conditions in urban water landscapes affect disease transmission and human health. The theme is particularly concerned with: Water-borne diseases Vector-borne diseases Infectious diseases Climate-related health risks Water quality Urban morphology Land-use changes Urban density Pathogen transmission Antimicrobial resistance The research takes a One Health approach, recognising the interconnected relationship between human health, animals and the environment. Researchers may investigate how changes in urban development, water management and environmental conditions affect the spread of infectious diseases. Example PhD research topics Antimicrobial Resistance Possible methods include: Microbiological sampling Cultural analysis Molecular analysis Resistance profiling Surveys Water quality analysis Transmission modelling Impact modelling Helminth Infections and Non-Communicable Diseases Potential methods include: Parasitological analysis Microbiological analysis Immunological analysis Clinical examinations Biomarker analysis Mouse models for mechanistic research Urban Microbiome and Dietary Ecology Potential methods include: Microbiome sequencing Dietary pattern analysis Metagenomic analysis Computational analysis Vector-Borne Disease Potential methods include: Climate monitoring Entomological surveys Temperature mapping Vector modelling Pathogen detection Potential supervisors Research Theme B includes: Prof. Dr. Christian Borgemeister Prof. Dr. Achim Hörauf Prof. Dr. Marc Hübner Dr. Indulekha Karunakaran Prof. Dr. Nico Mutters PD Dr. Marijo Parcina Dr. Manuel Ritter Prof. Dr. Marie-Christine Simon Dr. Nicole Zacharias Research Theme C: Governance and Institutional Change The Governance and Institutional Change theme is particularly relevant to applicants interested in policy, governance, economics, development studies, political science, institutional systems and public-sector transformation. This research theme examines how political, institutional and societal structures influence urban transformation and the ability of cities to respond to health and environmental challenges. Areas of interest include: Urban governance Water-health governance Public policy Institutional design Policy instruments Inter-sectoral collaboration Financing mechanisms Participatory decision-making Climate adaptation Population growth Unequal resource distribution Political economy Technological change Healthcare policy Institutional transformation The research seeks to generate evidence that can support more inclusive, transparent and adaptive approaches to urban development . Example PhD research topics Biodiversity-Based Bio-Economies Possible methods include: Economic impact assessment Policy analysis Value-chain analysis Cross-Sectoral Governance Potential methods include: Stakeholder mapping Policy analysis Governance framework development Case studies Urban Transformation and Pharmaceutical Innovation Potential methods include: Case study analysis Technology assessment Policy evaluation Innovation studies Political Economy of Health Equity and Technological Change Potential methods include: Political economy analysis Institutional economics Policy process tracing Case studies Impact analysis Urban Healthcare Policy Implementation Potential methods include: Institutional economics Case studies Impact analysis Microeconometric evaluation Climate-Responsive Health Policy Potential methods include: Policy mapping Infrastructure mapping Spatial analysis Policy evaluation Implementation research Economic impact assessment Potential supervisors Research Theme C includes: Prof. Dr. Katja Bender Prof. Dr. Jan Börner Prof. Dr. Anna-Katharina Hornidge Prof. Dr. Simona Helmsmüller Dr. Christoph Strupat Research Theme D: Adaptive Urban Ecosystems The Adaptive Urban Ecosystems theme focuses on how cities can plan and manage ecological and blue-green infrastructure in response to climate change and socio-economic transformation. Research areas include: Urban land-use systems Water infrastructure Nature-based solutions Ecosystem resilience Climate adaptation Circular economy Integrated water-resource management Biodiversity Urban soil management Ecosystem services Sustainable urban development This theme brings together engineering, ecological and planning perspectives to investigate how urban environments can be designed to provide multiple benefits for both people and ecosystems. Example PhD research topics Coupling Mechanisms of Urbanization Potential methods include: Hydrological modelling System-dynamics modelling Ecosystem-services analysis Biodiversity and Human Wellbeing Potential methods include: Biodiversity surveys Spatial data analysis Socioeconomic surveys Urban Soil Management Potential methods include: Soil sampling Soil biodiversity surveys Morphological identification Molecular identification Soil health indicators Spatial analysis Urban Decision Environments Potential methods include: Coupled ecological-economic systems modelling Collective learning dynamics One Planetary Health Potential methods include: Integrated modelling Framework development Systems thinking Commons governance studies Potential supervisors Research Theme D includes: Prof. Dr. Wolfram Barfuss Dr. Bibiana Betancur Prof. Dr. Lisa Biber-Freudenberger Prof. Dr. Mariele Evers What Does the PhD Programme Offer? Successful candidates will receive a structured doctoral research experience rather than simply conducting an independent PhD project. The programme provides several forms of academic and professional support. 1. Four-Year Doctoral Support Contract The Research Training Group will begin on 1 April 2027 . Successful applicants will receive a four-year doctoral support contract , with remuneration dependent on TV-L pay grade 13 at 65% , in accordance with the German public salary scale. Employment will be at either: University of Bonn; or Bonn-Rhein-Sieg University of Applied Sciences. 2. Funded Research Expenses The programme states that fieldwork, travel and related research expenses are fully funded . This is particularly important for doctoral projects involving international fieldwork or research in different urban environments. 3. Structured Doctoral Training Doctoral researchers will participate in an interdisciplinary training programme covering areas such as: Systems thinking Transdisciplinary research Academic communication Interdisciplinary research Research methods Soft skills Professional development 4. Interdisciplinary Research Environment The programme brings together researchers from different academic disciplines. This allows doctoral candidates to examine urban health challenges from multiple perspectives rather than approaching them from a single discipline. 5. International Research Network Researchers will have access to a strong national and international network involving universities and research institutions in Europe, Africa, Asia and Latin America. 6. Career Development Support The programme also provides dedicated career development support , structured supervision and clear progression criteria. Responsibilities of Selected Doctoral Researchers Successful candidates will be expected to actively participate in the Research Training Group and contribute to its interdisciplinary research environment. Their responsibilities will include: Participating actively in the RTG training programme. Taking part in interdisciplinary seminars. Conducting independent doctoral research aligned with one of the four research themes. Developing appropriate research methodologies. Collecting and analysing research data. Publishing research findings. Contributing to the development of Blue City concepts. Participating in transdisciplinary knowledge exchange. Developing systems-thinking and interdisciplinary research capabilities. Who Can Apply? The programme is seeking applicants who have already completed a Master s degree or equivalent qualification in a relevant discipline. The call specifically identifies a broad range of eligible academic backgrounds. These include: Agricultural and Food Systems Climate and Earth Sciences Development Studies Ecology and Life Sciences Economics and Management Mathematics Physics Computer Science Environmental Sciences Health Sciences Geography Infectious Diseases Hygiene and Infection Control Medical Microbiology Public Health Urban and Regional Studies Social Sciences Applicants should also demonstrate: A strong interdisciplinary mindset A clear interest in urban transformation Interest in the water-health nexus and/or urban health Excellent written English Excellent spoken English English Language Requirement Applicants are required to provide evidence of English language proficiency at B2 level , according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR), or an equivalent qualification such as TOEFL. Is the Opportunity Open to International Applicants? Yes. The programme has an explicitly international research orientation and involves partner institutions across Africa, Asia, Latin America and Europe . The call identifies partner institutions in Ghana, Togo, Cameroon, Brazil and Japan , while applicants are permitted to propose research sites in any Blue City worldwide . Therefore, the programme is not presented as being restricted to German or European applicants. Applicants should, however, ensure that they satisfy the academic, language and application requirements specified in the official call. Application Documents Required The application process consists of two stages . Applications will first be assessed by the RTG Selection Committee. Candidates considered among the most qualified will then be invited to participate in a virtual interview . Applicants are required to submit the following: 1. Curriculum Vitae A tabular-format CV should be provided, presenting the applicant s academic background, professional experience, research experience, skills and other relevant information. 2. Degree Certificates and Transcripts Applicants must provide: Higher education degree certificate(s) Full transcript(s) of records An explanation of the grading system used for previous studies 3. Motivation Letter A motivation letter of no more than 500 words is required. The letter should explain the applicant s motivation for joining the programme and demonstrate their interest in the relevant research area. 4. Research Exposé Applicants must submit a research exposé of no more than 1,500 words . This is an important part of the application because candidates are expected to propose doctoral research aligned with one of the programme s four research themes. 5. Interdisciplinary Research Statement Applicants must provide an interdisciplinary research statement of no more than 500 words . This should demonstrate their ability to think across disciplinary boundaries and connect their proposed research with the wider objectives of the Research Training Group. 6. Letter of Recommendation Applicants must submit one letter of recommendation . 7. English Language Certificate Applicants must provide evidence of B2-level English proficiency , such as CEFR, TOEFL or an equivalent qualification. Application Deadline The deadline to submit a complete application is: 19 October 2026 Applicants should ensure that all required documents are prepared and submitted through the online application portal before the deadline. Candidates should also indicate the specific research theme they are applying for. Important Information About Gender Equality The call states that, in accordance with the Landesgleichstellungsgesetz (LGG) NRW , women will be given preference in cases where candidates have equal suitability, qualifications and professional performance, unless reasons relating to another candidate prevail. The programme also states that it is committed to diversity and equal opportunity and is certified as a family-friendly university . Why the Blue City Concept Matters The Blue City concept is central to the programme. Rather than treating water solely as something that cities need to control, remove or supply, the programme examines water as an important component of the urban environment. This approach can involve examining: Rivers Coastlines Flood management Water infrastructure Public health Urban ecosystems Climate resilience Green-blue infrastructure Water quality Urban planning Social equity Disease ecology Governance The programme therefore recognises that water-related challenges cannot always be addressed through engineering solutions alone. They may also require changes in governance, public policy, community participation, health systems, environmental management and urban planning. Potential Research Opportunities for Social Science Graduates One notable aspect of this doctoral programme is its interdisciplinary structure. Applicants from social-science backgrounds can potentially find relevant research opportunities, particularly within Research Cluster C: Governance and Institutional Change . Relevant areas include: Cross-sectoral governance Political economy Health policy Institutional economics Policy implementation Climate-responsive health policy Urban transformation Technological change Stakeholder participation Institutional design This means that candidates do not necessarily need a medical or laboratory-science background to be relevant to the programme, provided their academic background and proposed research align with one of the eligible areas. Research Sites Can Be Located Worldwide Although the Research Training Group places particular emphasis on cities in the Global South , applicants are free to propose research sites in any Blue City worldwide . This provides considerable flexibility when developing a doctoral research proposal. Applicants could therefore potentially develop projects examining urban health and water-related challenges in different geographical contexts, provided the proposed research fits the programme s objectives and one of its four research themes. Application Process Applicants should follow these steps: Step 1: Select a Research Theme Review the four research themes: Urban Health Resilience Urban Disease Ecology Governance and Institutional Change Adaptive Urban Ecosystems Choose the theme that most closely corresponds to your academic background and proposed doctoral research. Step 2: Develop Your Research Idea Prepare a research proposal that addresses a relevant urban-health challenge and demonstrates a clear connection to the selected research theme. Step 3: Prepare the Required Documents Prepare: CV Degree certificate(s) Full transcript(s) Grading-system explanation Motivation letter Research exposé Interdisciplinary research statement Recommendation letter English-language certificate Step 4: Submit the Online Application Submit the complete application through the official University of Bonn application portal. Step 5: Selection and Interview The Selection Committee will evaluate applications. Shortlisted candidates will be invited to a virtual interview . Key Facts at a Glance Information Details Programme DFG Research Training Group “Urban Future” Main focus Urban health and transformations in Blue Cities Institution University of Bonn and Bonn-Rhein-Sieg University of Applied Sciences Opportunity Doctoral research positions Number of positions 10 Duration 4 years Start date 1 April 2027 Remuneration TV-L pay grade 13 (65%) Research expenses Fieldwork, travel and related research expenses funded Degree areas Multiple disciplinary faculties/Promotionskolleg NRW English requirement B2 CEFR, TOEFL or equivalent Application format Two-stage selection Interview Virtual interview for selected candidates Application deadline 19 October 2026 Research locations Any Blue City worldwide International focus Strong focus on Global South and international partnerships Conclusion The Urban Future DFG Research Training Group offers an interdisciplinary doctoral research opportunity for graduates interested in understanding how cities can respond to interconnected challenges involving water, public health, climate change, environmental sustainability and social equity . With 10 doctoral positions , a four-year support contract , funding for fieldwork and travel , structured doctoral training, interdisciplinary supervision and an international research network, the programme provides a research environment that brings together natural sciences, health sciences, economics, governance, social sciences, environmental research and urban studies. The four research themes— Urban Health Resilience, Urban Disease Ecology, Governance and Institutional Change, and Adaptive Urban Ecosystems —provide applicants with several pathways for developing a doctoral research project. Candidates interested in applying should carefully select the research theme that matches their academic background and research interests, prepare the required documents and submit their complete application by 19 October 2026 . title: African Development Bank and UNDP AI Hub Free Government AI Training 2026 for Public Servants
summary: The African Development Bank (AfDB) and the UNDP AI Hub for Sustainable Development, in partnership with Google and Apolitical, are offering a free, world-class artificial intelligence training opportunity designed specifically for government officials and public servants. The initiative aims to strengthen AI capabilities within the public sector, helping government professionals understand artificial intelligence, identify practical applications, manage risks, and support responsible AI adoption in government institutions. As governments across Africa and around the world increasingly explore artificial intelligence for public service delivery, policymaking, procurement, healthcare, climate action and organisational transformation, the programme provides public servants with practical knowledge they can use in their daily work. Applications are currently open, with a deadline of 30 September 2026 . About the Government AI Training Initiative The initiative is being delivered through the Apolitical Government AI Campus , a global learning platform focused on building AI capabilities within government. The African Development Bank is a founding member of the AI Hub s Executive Steering Group, while the UNDP AI Hub for Sustainable Development is partnering with Google and Apolitical to deliver public-sector AI capability building. The broader Government AI Campus seeks to prepare 1 million public servants to lead effectively in the age of artificial intelligence. The Campus is supported by Google.org and the Rockefeller Foundation and is designed to be technology-agnostic. This means that the training is not focused on promoting a single AI technology or platform. Instead, it helps government leaders and practitioners understand AI, use it responsibly and explore how it can contribute to better public-sector outcomes. The programme is particularly relevant as governments seek to close AI capability gaps and strengthen cooperation between the public sector, private-sector partners and innovation ecosystems. Why This AI Training Matters for Public Servants Artificial intelligence is increasingly being explored across government operations, including public administration, procurement, healthcare, climate policy, service delivery and strategic decision-making. However, effective AI adoption requires more than access to technology. Public servants also need to understand: What artificial intelligence can and cannot do How AI systems work How to identify appropriate government use cases The ethical and legal implications of AI Privacy and fairness considerations How to evaluate AI-generated information How to use generative AI responsibly How AI can improve public-service delivery How organisations can develop AI-ready workforces How governments can manage the risks associated with AI adoption The Government AI Campus seeks to address these capability gaps through accessible, practical and self-paced training. According to the programme information, 84% of Campus users say the training made them more effective at their jobs , while 87% say the training was relevant to their daily work . What Is Offered? Selected applicants will receive access to a curated set of courses from the Apolitical Government AI Campus. The training is designed to accommodate busy government professionals. Rather than requiring participants to attend scheduled lectures or live sessions, the courses can be completed online at the participant s own pace. Flexible and Self-Paced Learning The courses are: Fully online Self-paced Accessible from any device Designed without mandatory live sessions Not tied to a fixed class schedule Suitable for professionals balancing work and learning Most courses take approximately two to three hours to complete. Participants can start a course, pause their learning and return later. Their progress is automatically saved, allowing them to fit the training around their professional responsibilities. Core Courses Available Through the Programme The initiative features seven core courses covering different aspects of artificial intelligence and its application in government. Course 1: Understand How AI Impacts You and Your Government This introductory course is designed to help public servants develop a basic understanding of artificial intelligence without requiring prior technical knowledge. Participants will explore what AI is, what it can do, what its limitations are and why these issues matter for government. By completing this course, participants will be able to: Define artificial intelligence and explain its capabilities and limitations. Recognise the major benefits and risks associated with AI in the public sector. Identify ways AI can be harnessed for the public good. Explore how AI can contribute to improved public-service delivery. Discuss how public servants can use AI tools responsibly. This course can therefore serve as an entry point for public servants who are new to artificial intelligence. Course 2: AI Fundamentals for Public Servants — Opportunities, Risks and Strategies The second course provides a deeper examination of artificial intelligence. Powered by content from Stanford Online , the course explores how AI works, what its capabilities and limitations are, and how governments can approach AI adoption in a human-centred manner. The course also addresses issues surrounding trust, fairness, privacy, ethics and regulation. Participants will learn how to: Explain the technology behind artificial intelligence. Analyse trust, fairness, privacy and ethical risks associated with AI. Investigate the potential impacts of AI use cases through a human-centred approach. Distinguish ways AI can enhance government work. Apply lessons from AI experiments across different sectors. Consider regulatory frameworks relevant to AI. Explore strategies for responsible AI adoption within government. This course is particularly relevant for public servants who are expected to participate in discussions or decisions concerning AI adoption. Course 3: Effective Prompt Engineering for Public Servants Generative AI tools can produce significantly different results depending on how instructions are written. This practical course introduces public servants to prompt engineering , helping them communicate more effectively with generative AI systems. Participants learn how to formulate prompts, assess AI-generated responses and improve their instructions to achieve more useful results. The course enables participants to: Understand what prompt engineering means. Explain why effective prompting is relevant to government work. Construct effective prompts for interacting with AI. Critically evaluate AI-generated responses. Refine prompts iteratively to improve AI outputs. Apply generative AI more effectively to everyday professional tasks. For public servants already experimenting with generative AI, these skills can be particularly relevant to improving productivity and the quality of AI-assisted work. Course 4: AI Leadership in Government — Building Trust, Skills and an Innovative Culture This course is specifically tailored toward senior officials and leaders responsible for managing teams and shaping organisational culture. AI adoption is not solely a technology issue. Government institutions also need employees who understand how to use AI and feel confident and safe experimenting with new technologies. The course therefore focuses on the human and organisational foundations necessary for responsible AI adoption. Participants will learn how to: Describe the strategic value of AI for government operations. Understand the importance of an AI-ready workforce. Identify approaches for building a workforce that is informed and confident about AI. Develop a workplace culture that encourages innovation and responsible experimentation. Apply strategies for supporting AI adoption within organisations. Create a personalised plan for developing an AI-ready workforce. The course can be particularly relevant to managers, directors, team leaders and senior public officials involved in organisational transformation. Course 5: Smarter Procurement with AI Artificial intelligence has the potential to transform different stages of the public procurement process. This course examines where AI can potentially improve efficiency and impact within procurement while also addressing the risks associated with using AI in this area. Participants are introduced to practical frameworks for considering AI applications within procurement. The course covers: Fundamentals of AI and its application in procurement. Ways AI can address procurement challenges. Opportunities for optimising procurement processes. Ethical considerations surrounding AI in procurement. Legal risks associated with AI adoption. Real-world case studies and best practices. Initial steps for integrating AI into procurement environments. This course is particularly relevant to public officials working in procurement, contracting, supply-chain management and related administrative functions. Course 6: AI and the Future of Healthcare Systems The sixth course focuses on artificial intelligence within healthcare. Developed with SDA Bocconi School of Management , the course is designed for healthcare practitioners, regulators and policymakers who need to understand the opportunities and challenges presented by AI in healthcare systems. Participants will explore: The fundamentals of AI. Key characteristics and applications of AI in healthcare. Opportunities for using AI in healthcare systems. Challenges associated with AI-enabled healthcare. Ethical and regulatory considerations. Methods for assessing AI solutions. Responsible implementation of AI healthcare systems. Healthcare system AI readiness. Realistic timelines for AI integration. The course can therefore provide useful knowledge for professionals involved in healthcare policy, regulation, administration and technology adoption. Course 7: AI and Climate — Trade-offs and Transformation The seventh course examines the relationship between artificial intelligence and climate change. Powered by content from Stanford Online , the course explores how AI can support climate solutions while also examining the environmental costs associated with AI systems. Participants will consider how AI can contribute to areas such as resilient urban planning and the energy transition. Participants will learn how to: Explain why AI and climate change are increasingly interconnected. Understand how AI can contribute to climate and energy initiatives. Identify ways governments can support AI-enabled climate solutions. Recognise concerns surrounding the environmental impact of AI. Explore how public servants can contribute to addressing AI s environmental footprint. Understand the role governments can play in supporting greener AI development and adoption. This course is particularly relevant to public officials involved in climate policy, environmental planning, energy, sustainability and related areas. Who Can Apply? The initiative is open to current government officials and public servants who are working on issues connected to the implementation and adoption of AI in their countries. The opportunity is intended for public-sector professionals working across areas including: Public services Government administration AI implementation Digital transformation Public-sector innovation Public-private partnerships Technology policy Procurement Healthcare Climate and energy Organisational leadership Government strategy Applicants should be current government officials or public servants whose work relates to AI implementation, public services, partnerships or innovation. The information provided does not state a specific academic degree requirement, age requirement, gender restriction or professional qualification requirement . It also does not specify a particular nationality restriction within the eligible public-service audience. Eligibility, Qualifications and Geographic Scope Eligible Category of People Current government officials and public servants working on the implementation, adoption or responsible use of AI in their countries. Academic Qualifications No specific academic qualification is stated in the provided programme information. Professional Qualification Applicants should be current government officials or public servants. The initiative is particularly relevant to people involved in: Public-sector AI Government innovation Public services Public-private partnerships Digital transformation Policy and regulation AI-related implementation Countries and Continent The initiative is associated with the UNDP AI Hub for Sustainable Development and African AI development , and the wider programme is aligned with sustainable AI-driven growth in Africa. The information provided does not give a closed list of eligible African countries or state that applicants must hold a particular nationality. Therefore, applicants should consult the official application form for any country-specific eligibility requirements before applying. Key Benefits of the Programme The programme provides several potential benefits for eligible public-sector professionals. 1. Free AI Training The training is designed to provide selected applicants with access to courses from the Government AI Campus without the normal cost associated with professional learning programmes. 2. Practical Government-Focused AI Knowledge Rather than focusing solely on technical programming, the courses examine how AI can be understood and applied in real government environments. 3. Flexible Online Learning Participants can complete the courses remotely and at their own pace. 4. No Fixed Live Class Schedule Participants do not need to attend live sessions according to a fixed timetable. 5. Training Across Multiple AI Applications The curriculum covers AI fundamentals, prompt engineering, leadership, procurement, healthcare and climate action. 6. Responsible AI Adoption The programme places emphasis on issues such as privacy, fairness, trust, ethics, regulation and responsible use. 7. Public-Sector Leadership Development The leadership course provides senior officials with strategies for creating organisations that are better prepared for AI adoption. 8. Improved Workplace Productivity The programme reports that 84% of Campus users say the training made them more effective at their jobs , while 87% report that the training was relevant to their daily work . Why Public Servants May Find the Programme Relevant The growing adoption of AI means that public servants increasingly need to understand both the opportunities and limitations of AI systems. A government employee does not necessarily need to become a software engineer to benefit from AI knowledge. For example, an administrative professional may use AI to support document preparation and information organisation. A procurement officer may need to understand how AI could affect procurement processes. A policymaker may need to evaluate AI-related proposals. A manager may need to lead employees through organisational changes associated with AI adoption. Similarly, healthcare and climate professionals may need to understand how AI can be responsibly integrated into their respective sectors. The broad curriculum allows participants to focus on areas that are most relevant to their responsibilities. Programme Learning Format The Government AI Campus is designed around accessibility and flexibility. Participants can: Access the training online. Complete courses at their own pace. Use different devices to access the learning materials. Pause their studies when necessary. Return later and continue from where they stopped. Complete most individual courses within approximately two to three hours. This format makes the programme particularly suitable for working professionals who may not be able to commit to traditional classroom-based training. Deadline for Applications The deadline to apply for the African Development Bank and UNDP AI Hub Government AI Training initiative is: 30 September 2026 Applicants are encouraged to submit their applications before the deadline rather than waiting until the final day. How to Apply Interested applicants should complete the official application form provided for the initiative. Before applying, candidates should ensure that they meet the programme s eligibility requirements and provide accurate information about their current government or public-service role. Application Link and Official Website APPLICATION FORM: https://airtable.com/appbhi5ptYm0F6Gxx/paggZpgdfbdtZaJR5/form OFFICIAL WEBSITE: https://aihubfordevelopment.org/ For more training programs visit the OFY Website HERE DEADLINE: 30 September 2026 About the AI Hub for Sustainable Development The AI Hub for Sustainable Development is involved in initiatives designed to accelerate sustainable AI-driven development, particularly across Africa. The programme information describes the initiative as a G7-endorsed, MIMIT-UNDP co-led effort aligned with the Italy-Africa Mattei Plan . The AI Hub s broader programmes include initiatives focused on areas such as: AI infrastructure Compute readiness Voice AI Cybersecurity Sustainable AI development These programmes form part of broader efforts to strengthen AI infrastructure, skills and innovation ecosystems. Other AI Hub Programmes The AI Hub for Sustainable Development also lists several related programmes, including: AI Infrastructure Builder An initiative focused on developing AI infrastructure capabilities. Compute Accelerator Programme — Compute Ready A programme addressing compute-related readiness and AI infrastructure requirements. Voice AI Pathways An initiative focused on expanding voice AI applications to underserved communities. Cyber4Africa A programme focused on cybersecurity and related digital capabilities across Africa. Frequently Asked Questions Is this a scholarship? No. The opportunity is a free professional training programme , rather than a traditional academic scholarship. Is the training online? Yes. The courses are fully online and self-paced. Do participants need to attend live classes? No. The programme information states that participants do not need to attend live sessions or follow a fixed schedule. How long do the courses take? Most individual courses take approximately two to three hours to complete. Do applicants need previous AI experience? Not necessarily. The first course is specifically designed to explain AI in plain language and does not require prior technical knowledge. Can senior government officials participate? Yes. One of the courses is specifically designed for senior officials who manage teams and influence organisational culture. Is there a course specifically about procurement? Yes. Course 5, Smarter Procurement with AI , focuses on AI applications, risks and opportunities within procurement. Is healthcare covered? Yes. Course 6, AI and the Future of Healthcare Systems , focuses on AI applications and responsible implementation in healthcare. Is climate change covered? Yes. Course 7, AI and Climate: Trade-offs and Transformation , examines both the potential benefits of AI for climate action and its environmental costs. What is the application deadline? The application deadline is 30 September 2026 . Conclusion The African Development Bank, UNDP AI Hub for Sustainable Development, Google and Apolitical s Government AI training initiative provides public servants with an opportunity to develop practical knowledge about artificial intelligence and its application in government. Through the Apolitical Government AI Campus, selected participants can access a range of self-paced courses covering AI fundamentals, prompt engineering, government leadership, procurement, healthcare and climate action. The programme goes beyond simply explaining AI technology. It also addresses responsible AI adoption, including issues such as privacy, fairness, trust, ethics, regulation and organisational readiness. For current government officials and public servants whose work intersects with AI implementation, public services, innovation or public-private partnerships, the training provides a structured way to build relevant AI knowledge while continuing with their professional responsibilities. Applicants should review the official application requirements and submit their applications through the designated application form before the deadline. title: LabStart Fellowship 2027: Launch Your Climate Tech Startup With Funding, Mentorship and Access to U.S. Research Technologies
summary: The LabStart Fellowship 2027 is inviting entrepreneurs and aspiring founders with a passion for climate technology and entrepreneurship to apply for its next cohort. The program is designed to help entrepreneurs turn promising climate technologies and research into viable startups by providing funding, training, mentorship, access to technologies, and connections across the climate innovation ecosystem. Applications for the 2027 cohort are currently open , with a deadline of October 9, 2026 . LabStart focuses on bridging the gap between promising technologies developed in research laboratories and their commercialization in the market. Its program connects entrepreneurs with technologies, researchers, technology-transfer offices, industry experts, investors, and other stakeholders who can help transform an early-stage idea into a functioning climate technology company. What Is the LabStart Fellowship? The LabStart Fellowship is a climate technology entrepreneurship program designed to help founders move from an early-stage concept or technology opportunity toward launching a company. The program focuses particularly on deep climate technology , including technologies emerging from research laboratories and universities. Rather than requiring every applicant to arrive with a fully developed company, LabStart describes several situations in which its program can be useful. These include entrepreneurs who: Want to start a climate technology company but have not yet identified the ideal technology or business opportunity. Have identified a promising technology but need help obtaining a license. Have not yet raised capital for a specific product or technology. Are exploring a new market or innovative climate solution. Want to spin a technology out of a laboratory or university. Are looking for technologies to commercialize but have not yet identified the right market. The fellowship therefore focuses on helping entrepreneurs navigate the difficult journey between technology development, commercialization, company formation, and market entry . LabStart s Approach to Climate Technology LabStart s model is based on the idea that significant climate innovations can remain underdeveloped or under-commercialized when researchers do not have the entrepreneurial expertise, networks, capital, or commercialization pathways required to bring those technologies to market. The organization works with research laboratories, universities, technology-transfer offices, industry partners, and entrepreneurs to help close this gap. Its approach includes: Identifying promising climate technologies. Connecting those technologies with entrepreneurs. Helping founders evaluate market opportunities. Supporting intellectual-property and licensing processes. Providing entrepreneurship training. Connecting founders with mentors. Providing funding. Preparing companies for future investment and accelerator opportunities. What Does the LabStart Fellowship Provide? The current LabStart program provides a combination of funding, training, mentorship, technology access, and networks . The official program page describes the fellowship as a 12-month program with access to capital, capacity building, networks, and technology commercialization support. 1. Access to Capital LabStart provides milestone-based funding to support founders during the early stages of building their companies. The current program materials describe: $100,000 milestone-based funding on the program page. Full-time funding intended to give founders financial stability while focusing on their startups. Recent LabStart communications about the 2027–28 cohort have also referred to up to $125,000 in direct and in-kind funding , including support associated with the Discovery and Launch phases. Because the figures differ across current LabStart materials, applicants should check the latest program and application materials for the exact funding structure applicable to Cohort 2027. 2. Climate Tech Entrepreneurship Training Fellows receive training focused on climate technology entrepreneurship.
